# inbox-to-memory Lint Fixtures

The scopes the lint runs against, driven by [`tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh`](../../inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh). They are checked in rather than generated because the compatibility guarantees they encode are about files that already exist on someone's disk, and a generator would only ever produce files that match today's understanding of the old format.

- `old-only/` — the pre-v2 world: no `schema` key, block-style YAML lists, `related` as a nested mapping, bare line-ref anchors. Nothing here is ever migrated in place by a test; if a run modifies these files, the run is the bug.
- `mixed/` — both generations in one scope. This is the state the whole compatibility constraint exists to protect, and it is the default fixture for any check that claims to leave v1 files alone. Note `2026-01-13-atlas-cutover-readiness-JJuYgImRWn.md` is v2-shaped in every visible respect but carries no `schema` key, and it has to keep classifying as v1.
- `broken/` — one planted defect per file, so the failure count is a real assertion. A check that starts firing twice, or firing on the wrong file, shows up as arithmetic rather than washing out against a file that was already failing for another reason. The single memory record here is the exception: it exists so a contradiction flag has something accepted to point at, and it carries no defect.
- `journal-v1/` — one pre-v2 journal entry, which is the only place the nested `scope`/`path`/`note_id` source reference appears. The migrator flattens it to a compound string, and this is the fixture that proves it, including the report line for the `scope` sub-field the compound form has no room for.
- `scaffold-layout/` — the only fixture whose queue sits at `notes/_inbox/` instead of the scope root, which is what scaffold mode actually produces for a client or project. Every other scope here is flat, and that uniformity is what let the opt-in guard reject every scaffolded vault in the field without a single test noticing. Its contents are deliberately dull; the layout is the whole assertion.
- `cross-scope/` — one v1 note carrying four planted links, so the lint has to tell a link that leaves the scope from one that's dead. The path link into the sibling scope must pass, and the other three must fail as `link-broken`: a path link to a record that was never written, `../working-state`, which carries no id, and a bare link whose id matches only a file in the sibling scope.
- `cross-scope-elsewhere/` — the sibling scope those links point into. The smoke test never lints it on its own. Its two records are link targets: one the path link resolves, and one sharing an id with the bare link, so a bare link that passed would mean the id search had left `cross-scope/`.
- `split/`—the raw sidecar's scope, and it lints clean as committed. One v2 note is already split, with its raw text in `notes/raw/Kp3vR8sNq2.md`. A second v2 note still holds its raw text inline and links to the first, so `split-raw.sh` has one note to split and the link sweep has a target whose id matches a sidecar's name. The third note carries `body_schema: 1` and has to stay inline. The smoke test plants each raw-file defect and runs every split on a copy of this scope.

The four `.vtt` files feed `collapse-vtt.sh` rather than the lint, and each one pins a shape the collapser used to mishandle silently. `steerco-excerpt.vtt` is the regression baseline: hand-numbered cues, both speaker forms, and one unlabelled continuation line. `blocks.vtt` puts a NOTE, STYLE, or REGION block in all three positions one can occupy, before the first cue, between two cues, and after the last. `teams-export.vtt` keys its cues by `<uuid>/<n>-<n>`, the shape Teams and Zoom export, and ends on a cue whose only text is `42` so a spoken line that looks like an identifier has to survive as speech. `speakerless.vtt` carries no labels at all, which is what most machine-generated captions look like.

Migration tests copy a fixture to a temp directory first. Nothing under `tests/fixtures/` is ever migrated in place: if a run modifies a checked-in fixture, the run is the bug.

The mixed scope also carries two open-question slugs that recur across three notes each. One gets named out loud in the third note and becomes a deferred tension; the other goes unnoticed and becomes an unacknowledged one. Both branches of the recurrence rule need a fixture, because the interesting half is the branch where nobody in the room was tracking it.

The scopes are deliberately small. Every file here has to be readable in full while someone is debugging a failing assertion, so a fixture that grows past a screen has stopped doing its job.
